# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

Stats: 4 obs (2,044t read) | 27,677t work | 93% savings

### Nov 2, 2026
4 8:07p ○ ms parser unit architecture mapped in src/index.ts and README
5 " ◆ Microsecond units added to ms parser, README, and tests; 4 tests failing after first run
6 " ○ Microsecond parse failures traced to unmodified regex alternation in src/index.ts
7 " ● Microsecond regex alternation added to ms parser; full test suite passes
S3 Add microsecond support to ms (`us`, `µs`, `microsecond`, `microseconds`) so `ms("500us")` returns 0.5, with updated unit types, README unit list, and tests (Nov 2, 8:07 PM)
**Investigated**: The ms repository layout and src/index.ts parser: unit type unions, the parse regex, the parse switch with its `satisfies never` check, the README unit list, and the existing test files (parse.test.ts, parse-strict.test.ts, format.test.ts, index.test.ts).

**Learned**: Units are declared as string-literal unions, matched by a single regex in parse(), and mapped in a switch to millisecond constants. A scripted replacement anchored on a leading pipe silently failed because the regex begins with `(?<unit>`, which left the first test run returning NaN for microsecond input. A sed edit on the `<unit>milliseconds?` anchor fixed it.

**Completed**: Added a Microseconds type (`'microseconds' | 'microsecond' | 'µs' | 'us'`) to the Unit union in src/index.ts. Added the microsecond alternatives to the parse regex and a switch case returning n / 1000. Added a Greek mu (μs, U+03BC) case, since lowercasing the uppercase form produces it. Added the Microseconds type to the README units list. Added microsecond tests to src/parse.test.ts and a parseStrict case to src/parse-strict.test.ts. Verified with npx tsc --noEmit (clean), npx jest (171 passed, 100% coverage on index.ts), and npx biome check src (no issues).

**Next Steps**: Final review of the diff. The reported summary also notes that ms(0.5) still formats as "0.5ms" rather than switching to microseconds; that formatting behavior is intentionally unchanged and not part of the current request.

**Notes**: Two Greek-letter variants were handled deliberately: the micro sign (U+00B5) and the Greek mu (U+03BC). The case-insensitive regex flag and toLowerCase() can produce either form, which is why the matchUnit cast was widened. Earlier failures were a single root cause in the regex, not the type or switch changes.
